chunks: 2505 - Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Luqmān said to his son: When you travel with a people, then frequently consult them concerning your matter and their matters, smile often in their faces, and be generous with your provisions among them. If they call you, answer them; if they seek your help, help them; and adopt long silence, frequent salat (prayer), and generosity of soul with whatever you have of a mount, water, or provisions. If they ask you to bear witness to the truth, then bear witness for them, and exert your judgment for them when they consult you.

Then do not resolve upon a matter until you verify and consider. Do not answer in a consultation until you have stood, sat, slept, eaten, and prayed regarding it while employing your reflection and wisdom in your counsel. For whoever does not render sincere advice to the one who consulted him, Allah will strip him of his judgment and remove trustworthiness from him. And if you see your companions walking, then walk with them; if you see them working, then work with them; and if they give charity or offer a loan, then give along with them.

And listen to one who is older than you in age. If they command you regarding a matter and ask you for something, then say: Yes, and do not say: No, for 'no' is ineptitude and baseness. And if you become confused about the road, then dismount; and if you doubt the destination, then stop and consult one another.

And if you see a single person, do not ask him about your road and do not seek guidance from him, for a lone person in the open desert is suspicious. Perhaps he may be a scout for thieves, or he may be the Shayṭān who has confused you. And beware of two persons as well, unless you see what I do not see.

For the intelligent person, when he sees something with his own eye, recognizes the truth from it, and the one present sees what the absent does not see. O my son, when the time of salat (prayer) arrives, do not delay it for anything; perform it and take relief through it, for it is a debt. And perform salat (prayer) in congregation, even if upon the tip of a spear. And never sleep upon your mount, for that quickly harms its back, and that is not from the practice of the wise.

Unless you are in a litter in which you can stretch out for the relaxing of the joints. And when you come near the stopping place, dismount from your mount and begin with feeding it before yourself, for it is your very life. And when you intend to camp, then choose from the places of the earth that which is best in color, softest in soil, and most abundant in grass.

So when you dismount, perform two rakʿahs before sitting. And when you intend to relieve yourself, then go far away into the land. And when you depart, perform two rakʿahs, then bid farewell to the land in which you stayed and send salām upon it and upon its inhabitants, for every patch of land has inhabitants from among the angels.

key_terms.اسْتِشَارَتَهُمْ: seeking the counsel of one's companions in shared matters
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the obligatory salat (prayer), to be performed without delay
key_terms.النَّصِيحَةَ: sincere and faithful advice offered without deceit
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةِ: the angels associated with places and divine order
key_terms.جَمَاعَةٍ: congregation in which salat (prayer) is performed collectively
key_terms.دَابَّتِكَ: one's riding animal or mount during travel

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Luqmān teach about the etiquette of travel and companionship?
ai.summary: This hadith records Luqmān's advice to his son on the etiquette of travel, companionship, consultation, sincerity, and proper conduct in worship. It combines practical guidance with moral discipline, emphasizing salat (prayer), trustworthiness, service to companions, and careful judgment.
